For the Respondents: Mr. Anirudh Sharma, Advocate, for   applicant/respondent No.1.
 Mr. Jagdish Thakur, Advocate, for  _____________________________________________________________________ vs Miss Priyanka Gurnani And Ors on 4 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68135853/

 Mr. Surinder Saklani, Advocate, for   applicant/respondent No.3.
 ___________________________________________________________________________  Sandeep Sharma, J. (Oral)
By way of instant application filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, prayer has made for condonation of delay in filing the accompanying appeal, whereby applicant intends to lay challenge to award dated 3.11.2015, passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal -I, Solan, in MACP No. 27-S/2 of 2010.
2. Pursuant to notices issued in the instant application, non- .
applicant

/ respondent No.2-appellant-insurance company has filed reply, wherein prayer made by the applicant/appellant for condonation of delay has been seriously opposed on the ground that delay in filing the appeal has been not properly explained.

Apart from above, it has been further of stated in the reply that while filing application at hand, applicant has not approached this court with clean hands and has attempted to suppress the material facts.
3. rt Having

heard learned counsel for the parties and perused material available on record, this Court finds that Motor Accident Claims Tribunal below vide award dated 3.11.2015 while allowing the claim petition filed by the non-applicant/respondent No.1, though held the applicant/owner liable to pay compensation to the tune of Rs. 5.00 lac to the claimant, but ordered that at the first instance, amount shall be paid by the non-applicant/respondent No.2-appellant-insurance company and thereafter, same shall be recovered from the applicant.

After making the payment to the claimants, non-applicants/respondent No.2 filed execution petition in the competent court of law,
seeking therein direction to the applicant herein to refund the sum of Rs. 5.00 lac as ordered by the MACT Solan while passing award dated 3.11.2015.

In the aforesaid execution petition, repeatedly,
notices/summons were issued to the .
applicant/appellant, but on one pretext or the other, he failed to put in appearance.

Record reveals that on 22.11.2016, Process Server tried to serve the applicant/appellant at his residence, but he was not present at home, however, his wife who was present in the house, refused to take the of notice and apprised the Process Server that her husband had gone outside.
Again on 9.1.2017, Process Server attempted to serve the applicant, but he summons.
rt was not found at his residence and again his wife refused to receive the

On 2.12.2017, Process Server again visited the house of the applicant, but he was not present and his father, who was _____________________________________________________________________ vs Miss Priyanka Gurnani And Ors on 4 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68135853/
2 present at that relevant time, refused to receive the summons.
Finally on 15.3.2018, brother of the applicant received copy of the notice on behalf of the applicant, but yet applicant failed to put in appearance and as such, was ordered to be proceeded ex-parte.

Perusal of zimini orders passed in the executing petition suggests that counsel representing non- applicant/respondent No.2 apprised the executing court that parties are in process of settling the dispute and as such, matter was adjourned and finally on 8.12.2018, learned Lok Adalat Solan was informed that applicant JD has made payment of Rs. 6.00 lac through cheque as full and final settlement.

In view of the aforesaid statement, execution petition was .
dismissed as withdrawn.

4. Record reveals that on one hand, applicant was trying to settle the matter amicably with the non-applicant/respondent-appellant- insurance company, but on the other hand, he had filed appeal against the of award dated 3.11.2015 passed by MACT below, but since same was barred by limitation, present application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act was rt also filed.

There is delay of two years, seven months and seven days in filing the appeal and if the explanation rendered on record qua the delay is perused, there appears to be merit in the contentions of Mr. Jagdish Thakur, learned counsel appearing for the non-applicant/respondent No.2 that no plausible explanation has been rendered on record.

It has been stated in the application that while MAC petition was pending before the MACT Solan,
applicant had shifted to Darlaghat on account of his business and thereafter, he lost contact with his counsel.
It has
been stated that factum with regard to passing of the award came to his notice on 22.5.2018, while he was going to PGI and counsel met him near district court.

It has been further stated that immediately after having acquired knowledge with regard to passing of the award, he handed over the documents to his counsel, enabling him to file appeal, which is barred by the limitation.

Apart from aforesaid explanation, no cogent and convincing .
explanation qua delay has been rendered on record despite sufficient opportunity.

Repeatedly,
matter came to be adjourned enabling the applicant to render proper explanation qua the delay, but in vain.

5. Mr. Kulwant Singh Katoch, learned counsel appearing for the of applicant/appellant vehemently argued that factum with regard to decision intended to be laid challenge by way of appeal came to the knowledge of the rt applicant/appellant on 22.5.2018 and thereafter, appeal was filed within limitation and as such, objection of limitation raised by the Registry is not tenable and deserves to be rejected outrightly.

As has been taken note herein above, factum with regard to filing of the execution petition had come to the notice of the applicant on 22.11.2016, itself when Process Server tried to serve him at his residence and his wife refused to accept the notice.
This Court is unable to accept the submission made by the applicant that after having shifted to Darlaghat, he never visited his house at Solan where his entire family resides.
Even after 22.11.2016, on 27.12.2016, again notice was attempted to be served upon the applicant, but his wife again refused to take the notice.

On 15.2.2017, father of the applicant was found on the given address, but he also refused to take _____________________________________________________________________ vs Miss Priyanka Gurnani And Ors on 4 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68135853/
3 summons.

On 15.3.2018, finally notices were received by the brother of the applicant, meaning thereby, applicant was residing in a joint family, but .
repeatedly, family members refused to accept the notice.

Once notice was refused to be taken by the wife and father of the applicant, he was otherwise deemed to have been served, but even then,
learned executing court repeatedly, granted opportunities to the applicant to come present.

of 6. Having perused reports given by the Process Serving Agency on the summons/notices, as noticed herein above, this Court has no rt hesitation to conclude that factum with regard to filing execution petition had come to knowledge of the applicant/appellant on 22.11.2016 itself, but on one pretext or the other, he lingered on the matter.

On one hand, settled the matter with the non-applicant/respondent-appellant-insurance company by making the entire payment and on the other hand, approached this Court by way of appeal, which is barred by limitation.
Since there is no cogent and convincing reason assigned on the record qua the inordinate delay in filing the accompanying appeal, this Court sees no reason to allow the present appeal.
7. Needless to say, delay is not to be condoned mechanically, rather for that purpose, proper and plausible explanation is required to be rendered on record.

No doubt while deciding the application under Section 5 of the limitation act, courts are not expected to adopt hyper technical approach, but same time, it is also not expected to ignore the inordinate .
delay.

In the case at hand, neither there is proper explanation qua the delay nor applicant has approached this Court with clean hands, rather an attempt has been made to hoodwink the court by misstating the facts and as such, he otherwise deserves no sympathy from the court.
Explanation of rendered on record by the applicant is nothing but bundle of lies because same are contrary to the record as has been discussed herein above.

22.82.013, rt Hon'ble Apex Court in Civil Appeal Nos. 6974 and 9675 of 2013 dated in Basawaraj and Ors v. The Special Land Acquistion Officer, SLP (C) No. 6609-6613 of 2014 decided on 24.3.2014, Brijesh Kumar v. State of Haryana and Ors, Esha Bhattacharjee v. Managing Committee of Raghunathpur Academy 2013 (12) SCC 649 and Pundlik Jalam Patel (Deceased by LRs) v.
Executive Engineer Jalgaon Medium Project and Anr, 2008 (17) SCC 448,

8. Relevant paras of the judgment passed in Pundlik Jalam Patel's case supra, read as under:
"29.
It needs no restatement at our hands that the object for fixing time-limit for litigation is based on public policy fixing a lifespan for legal remedy for the purpose of general welfare.
They are meant to see that the parties CM no.776/2021 RP no.11/2021 do not resort to dilatory tactics but avail their legal remedies promptly.
Salmond in his Jurisprudence states that the laws come to the assistance of the vigilant and not of the sleepy.

_____________________________________________________________________ vs Miss Priyanka Gurnani And Ors on 4 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68135853/
4 30.

Public interest undoubtedly is a paramount consideration in .
exercising the courts' discretion wherever conferred upon it by the relevant statutes.
Pursuing stale claims and multiplicity of proceedings in no manner subserves public interest.
Prompt and timely payment of compensation to the land losers facilitating their rehabilitation/ resettlement is equally an integral part of public policy.

Public interest demands that the State or the beneficiary of acquisition, as the case may be,
should not be allowed to indulge in any act to unsettle the settled legal rights accrued in law by resorting to avoidable litigation unless the claimants are guilty of deriving benefit to which they are otherwise not entitled, in any fraudulent of manner.
One should not forget the basic fact that what is acquired is not the land but the livelihood of the land losers.
These public interest parameters ought to be kept in mind by the courts while exercising the discretion dealing with the application filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
Dragging the land losers to rt courts of law years after the termination of legal proceedings would not serve any public interest.
Settled rights cannot be lightly interfered with by condoning inordinate delay without there being any proper explanation of such delay on the ground of involvement of public revenue.
It serves no public interest."
9. Consequently, in view of the detailed discussion made herein above and law taken into consideration, present application is dismissed being devoid of any merits.
